target_customer: Beginner and retail investors in Vietnam, later commodities traders
problem: Vietnamese retail investors had limited easy access to stock investing, with high minimums and little social learning. Anfin offers fractional investing from about US$0.5 and in-app communities.

founders.name: Michael Do
founders.background_notes: Investment teams at several VC firms per e27, January 2022.

competitors.name: Finhay
competitors.traction_then: Notable startup in the space per e27
competitors.funding_then: Recently raised funding per e27, January 2022

competitors.name: Infina
competitors.funding_then: Recently raised funding per e27, January 2022

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage integration, fractional trading and social features on top of licensed partner brokers; standard fintech engineering with compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: Fractional trading and communities were copyable by Finhay and Infina; community effects were the hoped-for moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Anfin partnered with Eddid Financial in August 2023 and listed a commodity trading app.

market_need_then: Vietnamese retail trading accounts were growing fast in 2021 and regional peers like Ajaib and Mynt were unicorns, showing demand for app-based investing.

brand_strength.rationale: Regional startup press only; no source on mascot, community or brand-led growth.

outcome_analysis: Anfin raised three rounds within about eight months of launch, ending with a $4.8M pre-Series A in June 2022 co-led by YC, and has 40 staff listed. Competition from Finhay and Infina, which raised larger rounds, and Vietnamese regulatory scrutiny of investment apps in 2022 are the risks. No later round found.
